question: The refractive indices of two transparent media A and B are (3)/(2) and (4)/(3), respectively. The refractive index of medium A with respect to medium B is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**9/8.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refractive index** is the measure of the **bending of light** as it passes through a **medium.**
 
• The refractive index of medium A with respect to medium B can be calculated by **dividing **the refractive index of medium A by the refractive index of medium B.
 
• Therefore, the refractive index of medium A with respect to medium B is 3/2 divided by 4/3 = **9/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• How much light is** bent, or refracted,** as it enters a material is determined by its refractive index.
 
• In mathematical formulae and descriptive texts, the letter **n or n'** is most frequently used to represent the refractive index variable.
 
• The **velocity of light **of a certain wavelength in empty space, c, divided by its** velocity** in a substance, v, yields the refractive index, which is also equal to **n = c/v. **
